nodes.label: Software Design Specification
nodes.rationale: Working draft and minimal implementation blueprint. The FRS defines functional behavior and OpenSpec holds approved change requirements. If implementation details conflict with approved requirements, stop and resolve the discrepancy before coding.

nodes.label: Request Flow
nodes.rationale: React UI to API client to Express routes and middleware, then validation, application services, Prisma, and PostgreSQL. TanStack Query owns server state. Zustand holds transient client state. Business logic stays in application services so route handlers do not duplicate it. Public sharing uses a separate restricted read-only response path.

nodes.label: packages/shared
nodes.rationale: Only packages/shared owns cross-application types, API contracts, and Zod schemas, so the web app and API cannot drift. Shared schemas include one deterministic serialization procedure for the content-size check. The HTTP body limit must fit a valid 1 MiB document plus a bounded envelope and still stay capped.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 16 is the source of truth. Indexes cover owner-scoped note listing, trash cleanup, tag filtering, token expiry, share-link lookup, and a full-text index over title plus readable TipTap text. Unique constraints cover normalized email, owner-scoped tag identity, and the note-tag pair.

nodes.label: User
nodes.rationale: Stores id, email, normalized email, password hash, and timestamps. Normalized email is unique so registration identity does not depend on casing or surrounding whitespace.

nodes.label: RefreshTokenSession
nodes.rationale: Stores the user id, token hash, token-family or session id, expiry, and revocation timestamps. Hashing means a database read cannot replay a refresh token. Family tracking is what makes reuse detection revoke every session in that chain.

nodes.label: Note
nodes.rationale: Stores id, owner id, title, TipTap JSON, search data, timestamps, and deletedAt. Search data lives on the note so full-text indexing can follow create, edit, restore, and delete without a second content store.

nodes.label: Tag
nodes.rationale: Stores id, owner id, and name plus normalization fields. Uniqueness is per owner so two users can reuse the same visible tag name.

nodes.label: NoteTag
nodes.rationale: Associates a note and a tag with a unique pair constraint so the same tag cannot be attached twice and tag filters can join through one table.

nodes.label: NoteVersion
nodes.rationale: Stores the note id, a title snapshot, a TipTap JSON snapshot, and a creation timestamp. Snapshots are separate rows so history can outlive later edits of the current note.

nodes.label: ShareLink
nodes.rationale: Stores the note id, a secure token lookup or hash, expiry, revocation, and view-count data. The raw token is not the lookup key, so a database leak does not publish every live link.

nodes.label: PasswordResetChallenge
nodes.rationale: Stores a user or email reference, a protected OTP, expiry, attempts, and consumption or resend data. The OTP is protected rather than stored as plaintext so a database read is not itself a reset credential.

nodes.label: Error Contract
nodes.rationale: Every error is {error:{code,message,fields?}, requestId}. fields is optional. Clients never receive stack traces, secrets, or raw database errors. Status codes run from 200, 201, and 204 through 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 422, 429, and 500. 404 covers both unavailable and intentionally concealed resources.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Contract
nodes.rationale: Route paths, schemas, authentication requirements, and status codes come from the approved OpenAPI contract, delta-openapi.yaml during specification review. Implementation must not invent API behavior when the contract is silent.

nodes.label: Note Version Transactions
nodes.rationale: Create-plus-initial-snapshot, update-plus-snapshot, and version restore run in transactions so a failure cannot leave a note without its history or history without the note.

nodes.label: Scheduled Cleanup
nodes.rationale: An idempotent job removes expired authentication records and, after the 30-day recovery window, purges notes, versions, and share links. Idempotence lets the job run twice safely. Soft delete via deletedAt forbids physical deletion inside the window. Private operations authenticate and enforce ownership on the server. Passwords, refresh tokens, OTP secrets, and share-token secrets are never logged. Rate limits cover authentication, OTP, refresh, search, and sensitive writes.

nodes.label: Ticket Sequence
nodes.rationale: Approved order is AB-1001 project setup, AB-1002 authentication, AB-1003 OTP password reset, AB-1004 note CRUD and soft delete, AB-1005 pagination sorting and tag filters, then AB-1006 tags and counts, AB-1007 search, AB-1008 sharing, AB-1009 version history, AB-1010 authentication UI, AB-1011 notes list UI, AB-1012 TipTap editor and autosave, AB-1013 search UI, AB-1014 share modal, AB-1015 history drawer and restore, and AB-1016 Playwright journey. Ticket ids and scope stay as approved.
